figure.caption: Sketch the vector \vvec and one vector orthogonal to it.

solution.p: The vector \wvec=\twovec21 is an example of a vector orthogonal to \vvec.

statement.p: If a vector \xvec is orthogonal to \vvec, what do we know about the dot product \vvec\cdot\xvec?

solution.p: The dot product must be zero.

statement.p: If we write \xvec=\twovec xy, use the dot product to write an equation for the vectors orthogonal to \vvec in terms of x and y.
Use this equation to sketch the set of all vectors orthogonal to \vvec in .

solution.p: This is the line y=\frac12 x.

statement.p: An earlier section introduced the column space \col(A) and null space \nul(A) of a matrix A. If A is a matrix, what is the meaning of the null space \nul(A)?

solution.p: It is the set of vectors \xvec for which A\xvec = \zerovec.

statement.p: What is the meaning of the column space \col(A)?

solution.p: It is the set of vector \bvec for which the equation A\xvec=\bvec is consistent.
